
=================================================================
#88 Dangun & Old Joseon  (Long ago)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: Silla-Tang War · place: asadal · tone: founder fairy tale, then a dark legend
Logline: Before there are any kingdoms, there is a son in heaven who keeps looking down.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Before there are any kingdoms, there is a son in heaven who keeps looking down. He is **Hwanung**. His father **Hwanin**, the Lord of Heaven, notices, looks down himself at a mountain called Taebaek and the people living around it, and decides the world could use his son.
[1] [CARD Hwanin: The Lord of Heaven. He has been watching this peninsula since before it had names.]
[2] [DIAGRAM joseon-mandate Old Joseon · 고조선 — Heaven’s mandate made into a capital: Hwanin → Hwanung → Dangun → Asadal.]
[3] ¶ Hwanin does not plough — he opens the sky. Three seals go down with his son, so that nobody on the ground can mistake him for a prince playing at exile. Every later king in this chronicle will cut seals of his own, and every one of them is copying these.
[4] ¶ Hwanung lands on a mountain under the sacred birch. He names the ground beneath it the Divine City. Three thousand followers come down with him. Among them are the lords of wind, rain and cloud. Someone has to argue with the weather.
[5] [CARD Hwanung: Hwanung. A son of heaven who kept looking down until his father let him go.]
[6] ¶ From there he hands out civilisation in instalments. Laws. Punishments. Lifespans. Illness. Good and evil. Medicine. Three hundred and sixty matters in all. Somebody counted.
[7] ¶ There is a short way to tell the rest, the way it is carved on stones. The long way begins, as long ways do, with a bear who wanted something so badly that she outlasted a tiger for it.
[8] ¶ A bear and a tiger come to him and ask to be made human. He gives them a bundle of mugwort, twenty cloves of garlic, and one instruction: stay out of the sun for a hundred days.
[9] ── SCENE: The Sacred Birch ──
[10] ¶ The bear stays. She comes out a woman on the twenty-first morning, garlic still on her breath, and finds the mountain already staffed — wind, rain, cloud, and not one of them a husband. So she stands under the sacred tree. Not once. Every day, on the path he has to take if he means to reach the hall.
[11] [CARD Ungnyeo: Ungnyeo. Twenty-one days in a cave, and the tiger left first. A husband should be easy.]
[12] ¶ He means to reach the hall. On the third evening he gets as far as the birch, and the seal in his hand becomes a thing he is holding for no reason he can name.
[13] Ungnyeo: You're going to walk past again.
[14] Hwanung: …Not today.
[15] Ungnyeo: Yesterday you did. / And the day before. I was standing right here.
[16] Hwanung: I saw you. / The garlic reached this far.
[17] Ungnyeo: Twenty-one days of that, and this is what came out. / …I was going to say don't come closer.
[18] Hwanung: Too late. / Stay. I mean— don't go. Your hand—
[19] Ungnyeo: You already have the hand. / …Scared of the rest?
[20] Hwanung: I am. / Because you're looking at me.
[21] Ungnyeo: Then come down. / The tree can watch. I want… more.
[22] ¶ The kiss is clumsy. Beard, a new mouth, birch bark at her back. She makes a small furious sound and tries again, and the second one lands.
[23] ¶ White silk goes down among the roots. The fur at her throat opens under his mouth. She laughs once, startled at the sound, and pulls him down by the hair.
[24] ¶ By the time the moon clears the snow on the peak, the rust-red sash is somewhere in the moss, and neither of them has gone back up the path.
[25] Ungnyeo: …You're going already?
[26] Hwanung: I can't. / I don't know where I put the seal.
[27] Ungnyeo: Under my head. / I took it. …Don't go.
[28] Hwanung: …Thief.
[29] Ungnyeo: Marry me in the morning. / Right now I'm here.
[30] ── SCENE: Asadal ──
[31] ¶ Their son is Dangun. The name on the stone is Wanggeom: a king who governs, not one who inherits a bone rank. He founds Asadal where the mountain meets the plain. He rules for fifteen hundred years, and then he becomes the mountain.
[32] [CARD Dangun: Dangun. Half heaven, half bear, and all the paperwork of a first king.]
[33] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonder 1 — Old Joseon (Dangun); Ha & Mintz tr., pp. 32–33): He granted three heavenly seals and sent him to govern. Hwanung led a following of three thousand and descended under the sacred altar-tree on the summit of Mount Taebaek; this was called the Divine City. He married the bear-woman, and she bore a son named Dangun Wanggeom.❞
[34] [PLACE asadal: Where the mountain meets the plain, and the first crown met both.]
[35] ¶ Every later crown in these kingdoms argues, one way or another, back to the woman who used to be a bear. Her son’s city keeps his name long after he has become a mountain.
[36] ── SCENE: The Fall of Joseon ──
[37] ¶ Joseon outlives its founder by a long way. Two thousand years on it is still there, run by other kings now, from a walled city on the Taedong that has kept his name: **Wanggeom**. In the autumn of 109 BC, Han comes to the gate.
[38] ¶ It takes the empire of the West a year to take one fortress, and they do not take it. Wanggeom holds through a siege that begins in the autumn and is still going the following autumn.
[39] ¶ So they stop attacking the walls and start talking to the men behind them, which is cheaper and has never once failed.
[40] ── SCENE: The King's Wall ──
[41] ¶ **King Ugeo** has stopped sleeping in the palace. He sleeps on the wall, where he can hear the Han camp coughing, and his son, the prince, has started sleeping somewhere else.
[42] Prince Jang Hang: Father. They’ve sent terms again. / Open the gate, they say, and nobody inside gets hurt.
[43] King Ugeo: They said that last autumn. / Who brought it to you?
[44] Prince Jang Hang: …Does it matter who?
[45] King Ugeo: It matters. / Get off my wall.
[46] ¶ One of the ministers who have been doing the talking goes over the wall that week and dies on the road before he reaches the Han tents. Another does not bother with the road. One night at the start of summer he sends men up the wall-stair instead.
[47] Seong Gi: Majesty—!
[48] King Ugeo: …Seong Gi? / Don’t hold the city. Not for me. / Get the people out. Live… and make a new country. Anywhere.
[49] ¶ Seong Gi closes the king’s eyes, goes back up to the parapet, and holds the city anyway.
[50] ¶ He holds it until the dead minister’s son and the prince go down into the lanes, where people have been eating bark since the spring.
[51] Choi: The king is dead. / So who are you starving for now? Him?
[52] ¶ Before morning Seong Gi is dead too.
[53] ¶ Someone lifts the bar.
[54] The Herald: The wall did not come down.
[55] The Herald: A door was opened from the inside.
[56] ¶ Han takes Wanggeom. Some of the people the king told to live go south over the mountains. They settle in six villages around Surabol. Two generations later, they'll go looking for a king. The rest stay, and the empire cuts them into four pieces. The last piece is still collecting taxes four hundred years later.
[57] ¶ That is the story Munmu gets, in his mother’s version, with extra garlic. He came for the bear. He keeps thinking about the door.
[58] ¶ **Eight hundred years later, the empire comes back to the same river to do the same thing. This time, Goguryeo has a prince left…!**
